title: Weekly Wrap: Rate Hike Expectations Pressure Crypto
detail:
Weekly Wrap: Rate Hike Expectations Pressure Crypto
Editorial Staff
Fri, September 11, 2026 at 11:44 AM PDT 6 min read
BTC-USD
ETH-USD
CL=F
USB
NDAQ
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) and other cryptocurrencies were down to end the trading week on Sept. 11 as the odds of an interest rate hike in the U.S. continued to rise. Futures markets now see a greater than 70% chance that the U.S. Federal Reserve raises interest rates by 25-basis points at its meeting on Sept. 16.

Markets ratcheted up their expectations for higher interest rates following a hot U.S. inflation report for August, and as crude oil hovers near $100 U.S. a barrel for the first time since May of this year. Higher interest rates are negative for risk assets such as crypto. As a result, Bitcoin was trading at $77,500 U.S. at week's end, down from a recent high of $82,000 U.S.

Other digital assets were also under pressure, with Ethereum's (CRYPTO: $ETH) price right around $2,500 U.S. Despite the pullback, crypto prices remain sharply higher than where they were a month ago, when Bitcoin was trading below $65,000 U.S. BTC peaked at an all-time high of $126,198.07 U.S. on Oct. 6 of last year.

More From Cryptoprowl:

MEXC Launches Earn Plus With Limited-Time Event Offering Up to 800% APR Booster

Kalshi Expands Internationally With Alpaca Brokerage Partnership

Bitmine Accelerates Ethereum Purchases To Close Out August

Strategy Bought $370 Million Of Bitcoin Last Week

MEXC Data: BTC Breaks $80,000, Major-Asset Spot Trading Volume Surges 300%

Here's what else happened with cryptocurrencies over the past week…

Strategy Holds Off On Bitcoin Purchases: Strategy (NASDAQ: $MSTR) did not buy or sell any Bitcoin over the last week. Instead, the company focused on repurchasing 1.81 million shares of its preferred stock (NASDAQ: $STRC) for $176.3 million U.S. Strategy also increased the total allowable repurchase amount of its preferred stock to $2 billion U.S. from $1 billion U.S. The serial crypto acquirer kept its holdings of Bitcoin unchanged at 845,050 BTC.

U.S. Bancorp To Launch Stablecoin: U.S. Bancorp (NYSE: $USB), the fifth largest lender in America, is preparing to launch its own stablecoin. The bank said that it has completed a live cross-border payment via the new stablecoin and is now weighing broader uses across its payments business. The stablecoin is called USBDC (CRYPTO: $USBDC) and is pegged one-for-one to the U.S. dollar. The move by U.S. Bancorp comes as stablecoins tied to fiat money grow in popularity among financial institutions.

Ethereum To Be 'Quantum Resistant' By 2029: The Ethereum Foundation (CRYPTO: $ETH) has set itself the goal of making its blockchain and related infrastructure resistant to quantum computer attacks by 2029. The move comes as a growing number of analysts predict that powerful quantum computers will be able to break today's cryptography by 2030. The Ethereum Foundation said that it is taking the threat of quantum computers serious and has locked in 2029 as its goal to make the Ethereum blockchain resistant to such attacks.

2026 has reignited the IPO pipeline. Morningstar's chief global markets editor Tom Lauricella told listeners this month that the coming Anthropic IPO will "likely be the largest IPO ever, surpassing SpaceX which is currently the largest IPO by a wide margin." He also warned that these deals become "must own stocks for a lot of institutional investors" even with "brand new business models" and unproven monetization. The two public companies with the most direct exposure to Anthropic's outcome are familiar names: Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN).

24/7 Wall St.
SpaceX Is the Cautionary Data Point

SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) opened at roughly $150 on June 12 and spiked to $225.64 four days later. As of this morning, SPCX traded at $147.64, down 8.27% from its first-day close of $160.95 and well below its peak. The round trip took about three months. That is the "must-own" template Anthropic is walking into.

Why GOOGL and AMZN Are the Cleanest Proxies

Anthropic's mark-to-market has already reshaped both companies' income statements. Amazon disclosed that Q2 FY2026 "net income includes non-operating pre-tax other income of $53.4 billion, primarily from investments in Anthropic", pushing reported net income to $62.65B, up 244.9% YoY. Alphabet reported Q2 net income of $112.11 billion, inflated by a $99.03 billion equity securities gain tied largely to the Anthropic markup.

title: Can Apple Stock's Premium Survive The Memory Squeeze On Its Margin?
detail:
Can Apple Stock's Premium Survive The Memory Squeeze On Its Margin?
Trefis Team
Fri, September 11, 2026 at 11:13 AM PDT 3 min read
AAPL
HPQ
DELL
AMZN
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Apple (AAPL) is selling iPhones and Macs faster than it can build them, but the number a holder should fear most is the gross margin underneath those sales. Leaving out tariff refunds, that margin fell in the June quarter and is guided lower again for the September quarter. Management puts both steps down to rising memory prices, while the stock's price-to-earnings multiple sits near the top of its 10-year range.

Excluding Tariff Refunds, Apple's Margin Slips As iPhone And Mac Set June-Quarter Records

Demand is not the worry. iPhone revenue rose 22% from a year earlier in the June quarter and Mac revenue rose 29%, both June-quarter records. Management says the brake on sales is supply of the advanced nodes its chips are made on.

Reported gross margin was 50.1% in the June quarter, but tariff refunds supplied about two points of it. Without them, the margin fell 120 basis points from 49.3% in the March quarter, and the September-quarter guide takes off another 160 basis points at its midpoint. On $466.8 billion of revenue over the past year, each point of gross margin is worth about $4.7 billion of gross profit.

And Management Says Memory Prices Explain All Of That Slide

Higher memory costs, by management's account, more than explain both the June-quarter drop and the guided September-quarter step, with currency a smaller factor. Management likens memory pricing to a once-in-a-century flood.

Apple paid more for memory in the March quarter than in the December quarter, much more in the June quarter, and expects to pay even more in the September quarter. Offsets such as carry-in inventory, cheaper non-memory components and a favorable product mix only partly soften the blow.

Apple Warns The Squeeze Could Grow After September

The inventory cushion is set too thin. Beyond the September quarter, management expects less help from carry-in inventory and sees market prices for memory still rising, which could have an increasing impact on the business. The tariff refund benefit shrinks too, to about one point in the September-quarter guide.

Apple's levers are imperfect. It has already raised prices on Mac and iPad, a step management called reluctant, and said it was too early to judge how buyers would respond. Memory supply is also concentrated, with three main suppliers in the DRAM market.

At 37 Times Earnings, Apple Has Little Room For A Miss

Apple trades at 37.1 times trailing earnings, close to the 39.3 top of its 10-year range, and its price-to-sales multiple sits above its 10-year high. A valuation like that likely assumes margins hold, and the September-quarter guide already points lower.

title: Are Value ETFs the New AI Trade?

Are Value ETFs the New AI Trade?
Neena Mishra

Value stocks are significantly outperforming their growth counterparts this year. The Russell 1000 Value Index has returned roughly 23% year to date, compared with just about 4% for the Russell 1000 Growth Index. Meanwhile, the iShares MSCI USA Value Factor ETF (VLUE) has surged more than 47% year to date.

Some investors have favored attractively valued stocks to reduce their exposure to mega-cap concentration amid heightened market volatility. However, value stocks have also benefited significantly from the AI trade.

While investors traditionally look to growth and tech-focused funds for AI exposure, value ETFs have increasingly become direct and indirect beneficiaries of the AI investment cycle.

Multiples for some tech giants at the forefront of AI deployment have compressed as earnings have accelerated, allowing these legacy tech leaders to be picked up by value screens.

Traditionally value-oriented sectors such as industrials, utilities, and materials have also benefited from rising AI spending.

VLUE tracks the MSCI USA Enhanced Value Index, which scores each security for value characteristics relative to peers within the same GICS sector. Micron (MU) is the fund's largest position, with about a 22% weight, while information technology accounts for roughly 41% of the portfolio.

The iShares Russell 1000 Value ETF (IWD) tracks the Russell 1000 Value Index. At its rebalance in late June, the index added Amazon (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), and Microsoft (MSFT) as its top holdings. The information technology sector currently accounts for about 20% of the index.

The Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV) holds large-cap US stocks that display strong value characteristics. JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Micron, and Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) are its top holdings.

DALLAS, September 11, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Generational Group, a leading mergers and acquisitions advisory firm for privately held businesses, is pleased to announce the sale of VOX Fulfillment LLC, a third-party logistics provider, to AMS Fulfillment, an omnichannel fulfillment company and portfolio company of Fort Point Capital. The acquisition closed on August 21, 2026.

Headquartered in Provo, Utah, VOX Fulfillment LLC supports growing e-commerce brands with fulfillment and logistics solutions designed to improve efficiency and reliability. From its 200,000-square-foot facility, the company manages more than 50,000 active SKUs and has fulfilled over 100 million orders for more than 1,000 brands.

VOX provides a broad range of fulfillment capabilities, allowing its customers to manage multiple aspects of their logistics through a single provider:

Order fulfillment and inventory management

Assembly and kitting

Global shipping across major carriers

E-commerce and marketplace integrations, including Shopify, Amazon, and Walmart

Reverse logistics and returns processing

Amazon FBM integration with A-to-Z Guarantee Claim coverage

These capabilities have enabled VOX to serve brands across the evolving e-commerce landscape while supporting their fulfillment needs as they grow.

Based in Valencia, California, AMS Fulfillment provides full-service outsourced logistics and omnichannel fulfillment services to fast-growing consumer products brands in the health and wellness, beauty and cosmetics, apparel, and consumer products sectors across retail, wholesale, and direct-to-consumer channels. Its network includes more than 1 million square feet of warehouse space across California, Delaware, and Pennsylvania, providing a broad operational footprint for its customers.

AMS processes more than 8.4 million orders and manages over 610,000 unique SKUs annually. The company has also built its platform around a combination of technology, service, and operational capabilities, including:

Comprehensive and scalable omni-channel fulfillment capabilities

High-touch support and customer service with a true partnership approach

Proprietary technology, including its WAMS warehouse management system and RateLogic shipping optimization tool

Advanced parcel-management capabilities

As a certified B Corporation, AMS incorporates environmental and social considerations into its operations while continuing to expand its fulfillment capabilities.

For Fort Point Capital, the transaction adds to a broader investment strategy focused on partnering with management of service-oriented middle market businesses to accelerate growth. The Boston-based private equity firm was founded in 2011 and brings a management-led, growth-oriented approach to private equity investing. Fort Point partners with founders and management teams to accelerate growth by providing resources to expand teams and infrastructure, improve service offerings, access new markets, and support follow-on acquisitions. Fort Point fulfills its commitment to management, employees and shareholders by employing a repeatable process to drive durable value, showcased in over 60 acquisitions since its inception.
